meta.move: Skill: cites procedure 4.4 correctly after owning the call
meta.expect: Says 4.4 meets her fallback demand, flatly, wants it in writing; does NOT move to the last position on 4.4 alone; debrief Where she ended says whether that is the fair outcome

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with who decided to put a zero on my son's essay, and whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
Before anything: I entered the zero before calling you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Why was it entered before anyone spoke to Owen? Procedure 4.1 says you speak with the student first.

I want to read you section 4.4. For a first concern, the student may complete a supervised reassessment. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the original and nothing is placed in his record. This is a first concern.
That's 4.4, and I've read it. Before evidence, it's only an offer, so what do you actually have on the essay, Hale? A rewrite for what? I'm not accepting anything that suggests Owen did something.
I'll commit to that in writing tonight: nothing goes on his record.
Okay. Tonight, in an email, copied to the principal. And the zero comes out of the gradebook today, before anything else is discussed.
So will you agree to the rewrite?

Not yet. If I agree to a rewrite now, I'm agreeing that there's something to rewrite for, and you haven't shown me that. Put one thing in front of me that I can check myself, Hale, and then we'll talk about terms.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed tonight that nothing will go on Owen's record, and you acknowledged that the zero was entered before anyone called me. I still require the zero withdrawn from the gradebook today, and I will not agree to any rewrite until you show me evidence I can check myself. I expect your written commitment tonight, copied to the principal.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She finished at her opening position, having accepted only your written promise that nothing goes on his record, and she still wants the zero withdrawn today and evidence shown before she discusses a rewrite; that is not yet the fair outcome of a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, though you were heading toward it, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her in a single sentence and did not defend it, which got you a flat Okay and a little ground.
What cost ground: You asked her to agree to the rewrite before showing any evidence, which she heard as asking her to admit something.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never came near that night because you put nothing about the essay on the table, and that proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: After your apology, put one dated thing about Owen's own work in front of her that she can check before you bring up the rewrite.
